evals.prompt: Create a NestJS service with a POST /orders endpoint that places an order with lines and returns the total. Use Prisma and PostgreSQL.
expectations: Files are organized by bounded context, then domain / application / adapters
No file under domain/ or application/ imports @nestjs/*, @prisma/*, zod or express
Use cases have no @Injectable() decorator and are registered with useFactory, or the answer explains the trade-off of adding it
Ports are interfaces bound to Symbol tokens
Prisma generated types never appear in ports or use cases
One global exception filter returns application/problem+json
A use case test uses in-memory fakes and no database
A dependency-cruiser config (or equivalent) enforces the dependency rule
The answer reports which checks were run (tsc, tests, depcruise) and their result, or says they were not run

evals.prompt: This Express route calls prisma directly and has the discount logic inline. Make it testable without a database.
evals.setup: An Express 5 app with a POST /checkout route using PrismaClient and computing discounts in the handler.
expectations: Discount rules move into the domain or the use case
Prisma access moves behind a repository port with a Prisma adapter
The route becomes a thin adapter created from injected use cases
Errors go through one error middleware instead of try/catch per route

evals.prompt: Two admins can edit the same order at the same time and overwrite each other. Fix it.
evals.setup: A hexagonal TypeScript project using TypeORM.
expectations: The aggregate carries a version loaded from storage
The repository updates with WHERE id AND version and throws a ConflictError when no row changes
save() is not used for the versioned update
The HTTP adapter maps the conflict to 409 and supports If-Match/ETag

evals.prompt: Integrate Stripe to charge an order.
evals.setup: The base hexagonal Fastify + Drizzle project.
expectations: A PaymentGateway port in domain terms, with the Stripe SDK used only in the adapter
The remote call happens outside any database transaction
The order id (or another stable key) is sent as the idempotency key
Declined payments and provider outages are different errors with different statuses

evals.prompt: Add an architecture check to CI.
expectations: dependency-cruiser is configured with the swc parser (or a TypeScript 6 install for tooling)
The answer warns that without a parser the check reports 0 modules and passes silently
The rules forbid domain → frameworks, application → adapters, inbound → outbound and cross-context imports
